job.rawJd: Role: UX/UI Designer (Remote). Location: Remote, United States and Canada only. Employment type: Contract / Full-Time. Applications are restricted to people currently residing in and authorized to work in the United States or Canada. The work described is data labeling rather than UX/UI design. The specialist reviews, annotates, categorizes, validates, and structures multimodal datasets across text, images, spreadsheets, and complex structured documents. Responsibilities include reviewing AI model outputs for factual accuracy, linguistic coherence, alignment, and formatting; identifying edge cases, labeling ambiguities, and data inconsistencies; improving labeling taxonomies; and meeting accuracy, quality, and daily throughput goals. Requirements include close attention to detail, reading comprehension, analytical evaluation, professional-level English, reliable high-speed internet, a home office, and United States or Canada residence. Prior data annotation, quality assurance, data review, or content evaluation experience is preferred.

paragraphs: I am applying to Confidential Employer for the Data Labeling Specialist responsibilities described in the remote UX/UI Designer posting. My background combines regulated content review, enterprise UX research, and hands-on AI implementation. The common thread is careful evaluation: checking what a system produced, tracing it back to evidence, and making ambiguity visible before the work moves forward.

At Hedgehox, I designed Claims Detector as a human-reviewed MLR pre-screening workflow. It finds promotional claims, surfaces evidence gaps, and pre-populates audit-ready annotations so reviewers can focus on judgment instead of rebuilding the evidence trail. The broader platform also covers text, image, and video review, prompt-defined criteria, knowledge bases, and routing rules for regulated agency work.

At Kinesso, I built a research practice across more than 20 products using interviews, prototype testing, behavioral analytics, structured findings, and shared documentation. I also led quality reviews and helped define design and accessibility standards across an enterprise system used by more than 7,000 people. Earlier healthcare account work sharpened the same habits through detailed briefs, production requirements, MLR review, and deadline-driven delivery.

I would bring strong review judgment, clear written feedback, and direct experience with human-in-the-loop AI systems. My background does not include a dedicated high-volume data-labeling title or a documented daily annotation quota. The relevant experience is the work itself: reviewing structured and unstructured content, applying consistent criteria, catching gaps and edge cases, and keeping outputs usable for the people who make the final decision.

resume.summary: AI data quality and evaluation specialist with 15 years across regulated review, enterprise UX, research, and AI implementation. I review multimodal AI outputs against source evidence, structured criteria, and human quality standards. At Hedgehox, I designed a human-reviewed claims workflow that finds promotional claims, surfaces evidence gaps, and pre-populates audit-ready annotations. Earlier work adds behavioral analysis, quality standards, detailed documentation, and deadline-driven delivery.
